**Manage Projects To Perfection**

Big dreams turn into bigger results with a killer project plan. Use this basic structure to build your team's ideal workflow, for projects big or small.

Here's what's included, and how to get this project management party started:

1. **Resources (Start Here!):**
This list is perfect for you and your team to have all those documents, specs, designs, or anything you tend to reference all the time. Meeting schedules and answers to common questions are also recommended to pop into this list so that your team is informed at all times. 📚

2. **Questions For Next Meeting:**
Never again forget that important question you thought of in the shower this morning! Slide your Q's into this handy list so your team keeps on flowing. 🌊

3. **To Do:**
The mother of all lists—the good ol' To Do. This is where assigned tasks live so that your team can see who's working on what and when it's due. Crystal clear all day, week, and month. 🔮

4. **Pending:**
We all have those in-between tasks that are technically done but also awkwardly waiting for another step. That's where the Pending list comes into play, use this list to share what those next mini-steps are with your team. 💬

5. **Blocked:**
With any successful project comes at least one inevitable blocker. Splash those red-tape, blocking issues that are slowing your team down so you can tackle it in the best way; together. 🚷

6. **Done:**
Our favorite list, the Done list. Stop, drag, and drop! For all your finished tasks that your team has hustled on and feels proud of. ✨

@palhonti1 @tshaks @ricardobonfim18
Hello, this what I’ve wrote to Pál, Ricardo and Mosima, but since Ricardo is the main contact point to the dev team, please follow his instructions, I don’t want to mix up things, I just copy here what I’ve wrote:

”Same data point are applied as in the previous challenge, but becuase this challenge requieres more "legwork" (for exploring and mapping), we could see a change in volunteer hours. If the system can take it, we can add number of identified vulnerable housholds and residents, but I feel this is the "nice to have" section now.

**CH-012, Garden & Soil Rescue** -- the conversion factor here (1.5L/m²/week) is a bit similar to the CO2e in the compost challenge, it is a very conservative rule of thumb metric which will not stand without proper expert review. The water-saving effect of mulch depends heavily on climate, soil type, irrigation regime, mulch material, and mulch depth, so it is very complex issue, but one thing is for sure, that mulching is good and helps. For now I don't have a better answer to this open question.

If there is a professional gardener is involved teaching the circle on how to mulch, we can add a differentiated metric proposed by Giovanni in the[ impact framework V4](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1_Jg4RCQH9dedMzHiULJ7VH3j_eGvfi_b/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=111091607497601050872&rtpof=true&sd=true "‌"), in the Participation section as knowledge transfer hours, but again, this is the "nice to have" part. So participants, volunteer hours and area mulched is a must. As in the master spec document, there is a section for techniques, if they mulch a bigger or different areas are mulched in different ways, that can be counted too.

**CH-015, Urban Greening** -- exact  surface temp. reduction factor needs expert review. I did a quick research, and for now we can also go with a conservative rule of thumb calculation (not hard fact!), that for 1 m2 removed "grey" surface replaced by "green" surface could reduces surface (and not air) temperature by 8-12 degrees Celsius.

Prevously we had some discussion about the accounting for greened areas with Pál, and I still think that if possible we could have different metrics for areas where concrete was removed and where planting happened, even if it is the same area. Why? Because in a lot of time these actions require approval from some authority, private owner, the municiplaity etc., so asphalt removel happens in one time, and greening happens later, but good deeds are already done which should be measured and showcased. But I have to emphasize again, that further expert review is requiered to compare and match the existing calculations, because there are different standards for this, not to mention the exact meaasurements. Of course if a heat mapping challenge is linked to this, we would have citizen science data on this, if a circle decides to take on these challenges at the same time.

I can see that **CH-016, Community Garden** metric formula is currently TBD. We have plenty of things to measure here and data to collect, the easieast and most important metric is the area, m2.”

Transform passive viewers into active community participants with Circles

Once a Guardian joins:

- They can follow activities and see impact

- Sense of contribution

Challenges connect digital participation with real-world organizing.

Members should be able to:

- Contact facilitators
- Join WhatsApp groups
- Access external Circle communication channels

A Guardian:

- Can leave a Challenge
- Remains part of the Circle unless removed manually

A Guardian cannot:

- Leave a Circle while participating in active Challenges supported by it

Challenges are composed of Steps (Activities need to complete that challenge defined in the template)

- View Steps status
- Read Steps instructions
  - Understand expected actions
  - Understand evidence requirements
  - Understand expected impact

Not every member needs evidence permissions to participate operationally in the field.

## **Goal**

Create the main participation and mobilization experience.

This is one of the most important flows in the Pilot.

---

## **Discovery Logic**

Users may arrive through:

- Explore-UI
- (priority) Shared links
- Circle Challenge Lists

---

## **Challenge View Logic**

The Challenge page should:

- Explain the Challenge clearly
- Explain the Circle supporting it
- Show current status and impact
- Provide guidance and steps
- Show Activities timeline
- Encourage participation (share external Circle's channels)
- Allow copying a sharing link

If the user is not authenticated:

- Joining triggers Account Creation flow

Once joined:

- User becomes a Challenge member
- User also becomes part of the supporting Circle

cards.desc:
## **Goal**

Transform passive viewers into active community participants with Circles

---

## **Logic**

Once a Guardian joins:

- They can contact (external link) the facilitator
- They can follow activities and see impact
- They can connect to local mobilization channels

The member experience should reinforce:

- Sense of contribution
- Visibility of progress
- Community belonging

---

## **External Community Connection**

Challenges connect digital participation with real-world organizing.

Members should be able to:

- Contact facilitators
- Join WhatsApp groups
- Access external Circle communication channels

---

## **Membership Rules**

A Guardian:

- Can leave a Challenge
- Remains part of the Circle unless removed manually

A Guardian cannot:

- Leave a Circle while participating in active Challenges supported by it

---

# **(Core) Flow  — Understand what should be done ( Steps)** 

## **Goal**

Help members understand how to contribute.

---

## **Logic**

Challenges are composed of Steps (Activities need to complete that challenge defined in the template)

Members should be able to:

- View Steps status
- Read Steps instructions
  - Understand expected actions
  - Understand evidence requirements
  - Understand expected impact

Not every member needs evidence permissions to participate operationally in the field.

---
